recipes.name: Awesome Eggplant Rollatine
ingredients_raw: 1 (10 ounce) package frozen chopped spinach, thawed and drained
1 (28 ounce) jar tomato pasta sauce, divided

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
In a shallow mixing bowl combine 3 eggs, 1 tablespoon garlic powder, 1 cup Parmesan cheese, Italian seasoning, salt and pepper. In a separate, shallow dish or plate, pour the flour.
Heat oil in a large, deep skillet. Dredge eggplant slices in flour, then in egg mixture and fry slices 2 or 3 at a time in hot oil. Place fried slices on a paper towel lined plate to drain.
In a large bowl combine ricotta, 1/2 cup mozzarella, remaining 1 cup Parmesan, remaining 1 tablespoon garlic powder, 1 egg, parsley and spinach; mix well.

Spread about 1/3 of the pasta sauce in the bottom of a 9x13 inch baking dish. Place about 2 tablespoons of spinach mixture in the center of each eggplant slice and roll securely; place in prepared pan. Pour remaining pasta sauce over eggplant rolls and top with remaining 1/2 cup mozzarella cheese.
Bake in preheated oven for 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Awesome Eggplant Rollatine
raw_recipe.description: Thinly sliced eggplant is lightly fried, then stuffed with a spinach and cheese mixture and baked with pasta sauce and mozzarella cheese.

video.description: If your family loves Italian food, you’ll love this pasta-free dish full of eggplant, spinach, pasta sauce and cheese. Dredge long slices of eggplant in flour and a mixture of eggs, garlic powder, Parmesan cheese and Italian seasoning, then fry. Roll the fried eggplant slices around a cheesy mixture of ricotta, mozzarella, Parmesan, garlic powder, egg, parsley and spinach. Place the rolls along with plenty of pasta sauce into a baking dish, top with more mozzarella, and bake until bubbly, hot, and ready to eat.

review.reviewBody:
It should be noted that when you slice the eggplants, make sure you are slicing them lengthwise (not width-wise like my fiance did) :) Also, I would recommend instead of frying the slices, bake them on a cookie sheet w/ a layer of olive oil at 350 degrees for about 15 min. 
I also used fresh garlic instead of garlic powder. Good recipe.

This is so good, but a lot of work, so I modified it. Instead of dredging in flour and then the egg/cheese mixture, I omit the flour altogether and just dredge the eggplant in egg, then in the cheese/spices mixture before frying. Instead of rolling it up, I just layer slices in the pan (with some sauce in the bottom of the dish) and put the cheese/spinach mixture on top, and then cover with the remaining sauce. It's truly awesome!

Made this as an "Eggplant Lasagna" last night and it was fantastic! I sliced the eggplant lengthwise on a mandolin about 1/4" thick then did a flour, egg, breadcrumb coating (breadcrumbs mixed with garlic powder, onion powder, and Parmesan Cheese). Layer like a lasagna - sauce, fried eggplant (overlapping a little), cheese mix (15 oz. Ricotta, 8 oz. Mascarpone, mozzarella, provolone, and 10 oz. spinach- squeezed dry), sauce, sprinkle of mozzarella, then repeat. I browned a pound of Italian sausage and 1/2 the lasagna also had sausage (on top cheese mix). Final layer of fried eggplant and plenty of mozzarella/provolone on top! Baked at 375 degrees about 40 minutes but had to cover about 1/2 way to prevent overbrowning. Can't wait to have leftover tonight as the fridge smells so good when opened... Thank you so much for posting this!

The batter is very thick I added an extra egg and then I used two more eggs and salt to wash my remaining eggplant when the breading mixture ran out. My eggplant was thin so I just layered the sauce then eggplant then cheese then eggplant cheese and a but of sauce and cheese on top. I also think two tablespoons of garlic powder may have been a little heavy handed maybe I'd just use a 2-3 cloves of fresh next time.

Have made this numerous times and love the way the eggplant comes out and rolls so easily. As others have mentioned, the egg mixture is very thick. I've added egg whites to the eggs and would start with 1/2 cup of Parmesan versus 1 cup. When I made it following the recipe, still had to add either water or egg whites to mixture to get through the frying, and would squeeze/wipe off (with my fingers) the heavy mixture to give it a finer coating. They come out excellent. Also add pesto to my ricotta mixture, and people have raved about it. Good jumping off recipe to make it your own.

A great recipe! I made a few changes based on other reviewers' tips. For the eggplant, just an egg wash followed by a Parmesan, herb, garlic, and flour mixture. Although I fried the eggplant this time, next time I'd infuse some olive oil with garlic and herbs, lightly coat the eggplant, and roast the slices to make it healthier. The eggplant flavor was muted. I used one large eggplant (cut 3/16" thick, lengthwise), 2 eggs in egg wash, the full recipe of filling, and homemade sauce. It is time and labor intensive, but no more than expected for a recipe like this. Certainly, I'd recommend trying it and customizing it to your tastes.

This was delicious and beautiful. 3 things: 1) Cut the peeled eggplant lengthwise into thin strips with a slicer; 2) Use 3 bowls instead of 2 - one for flour, one for egg, the other for parm cheese (& I added bread crumbs); 3) I pan fried the eggplant (& it was delicious), but I can see why some folks opt to bake it to cut the calories. When it came out of the oven, it was beautiful & did I mention delicious :>)

OK...I am doing something I swore I wouldn't. I am reviewing a recipe after making some serious changes to it first.

The first step of coating the eggplant and frying sounded like too much work...so I just peeled the sides of the eggplant, made slices perpindicular to those peels (so that the eggplant would retain skin on the edges only). Then, I brushed olive oil, salt and peeper on each side and roasted in the oven on two baking sheets @ 350 for 15 minutes, turning the slices halfway through and switching the baking sheets on the racks.

I added marjoram (not a fan of oregano), garlic and nutmeg to the cheese mixture and proceeded with the roll-up and the sauce. 

SPECTACULAR!

I will be making this EASY, EASY dish again and again...perhaps adding some browned Italian sausage or cooked diced chicken to the filling for variety.

WONDERFUL!

Excellent! I loved this recipe, althought I changed it a little. I dipped the eggplant in flour, then egg/water mixture, then in parmesan cheese mixture (where I substituted a sundried tomato/basil/oregeno combo for italian seasoning, and then fried them in my deep fat frier. I also layered the eggplant, like lasagne, using spaghetti sauce with italian sausage in it, and adding mushrooms. It was delicious! I did not find it to be overly time consuming (about 30 minutes of prep, and 30 minutes of baking) but the end result made it worth it. This is definitely a keeper.

I love this recipe.....however the batter was too thick and not enough for the 2 large eggplants we had. We ended up adding another half batch and adding a little beer to mixture to thin it out a bit.

This was wonderful, alot of work but worth it, I tried baking eggplant in oven, never got level of crispness I wanted, ended up using canola oil and crisping them up in a skillet.Loved the spinach in it which I used fresh chopped not frozen, and a little extra cheese. Yummmm

Very good recipe! My wife who often orders eggplant rollatini out said it was some of the best she ever had. Only change to the recipe was that I thinned the egg batter with some water as some reviewers had suggested was too thick. I tried cooking in the oven on a baking sheet coated with olive oil. The eggplant result was OK, however much of the coating came off and cleaning the cookie sheet was a pain.
This was delish. I added angel hair pasta with meat sauce since the dish didn't call for any meat. It was not necessary.
I added sun dried tomato spread. I add this to all recipes with tomato products.
Very tasty!!
This was delish. I used the air fryer for the eggplant and added mushrooms. I’d make this again!
We loved this recipe. We did make the changes recommend and just layered it like lasagna. The leftovers the next day were just as good if not better! Nothing leftover here!
This was a tasty blend of eggplant parmigiana and lasagna. A lot of work and mess, but overall, worth it. Next time I'll take other reviewer suggestions and bake instead of fry
Not really happy with this one

The flavor of this recipe is wonderful. Just make sure your egg/Parmesan dredge is thin and not to thick or it won't stick. also my eggplant slices were to small to roll so I made it into a lasagna. my husband loved it. He said the spinach was a different twist.
